##Rationale and Introductions

Wildfires are a pressing environmental challenge in California that has been exacerbated by decades of fire suppression, increasing drought conditions, and a changing climate. This dataset contains wildfire data for the past 75 years, offering a unique glimpse into how fire patterns have shifted over time. This report focuses on how climate change has impacted wildfires, with increasingly intense droughts contributing to larger fires, or with increased frequency of storms potentially causing more fires via lightning striking dry fire fuels. By providing statistical evidence that wildfire or lightning strike intensity has increased over time, this research can inform policy recommendations, ideally encouraging more proactive fire management strategies such as prescribed burning to reduce fuels.

##Research Questions
1. Has the size of California wildfire burn areas of changed over time?
2. Has the frequency of California wildfires caused by lightning strikes changed over time?

##Dataset Information
This dataset is sourced from the California Natural Resources Agency GIS database and is serviced by the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection’s  CAL FIRE eGIS. It includes layers that subset from the larger dataset according to year the fire occurred, and size of the burn area in acres. It contains 17,540 records, spanning from the 1950s to May 9, 2025. It is a publicly available feature layer and was last updated on May 9, 2025.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
#loading packages 
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(here)

#set working directory
here()
```

```{r data wrangling, include=FALSE}
#reading in data
CA_fires <- read.csv(file=here(
  "Data/raw/California_Historic_Fire_Perimeters_1516624541847049096.csv"), 
  colClasses = c('Cause' = 'factor',
                 'Collection.Method' = 'factor',
                 'Management.Objective' = 'factor',
                 'State' = 'factor',
                 'Agency' = 'factor',
                 'Unit.ID' = 'factor'))

#formatting date columns
CA_fires$Alarm.Date <- mdy_hms(CA_fires$Alarm.Date)
CA_fires$Containment.Date <- mdy_hms(CA_fires$Containment.Date)

CA_fires <- CA_fires %>%
  mutate(Cause = recode(Cause, 
                        "1" = "Lightning",
                        "2" = "Equipment Use",
                        "3" = "Smoking",
                        "4" = "Campfire",
                        "5" = "Debris",
                        "6" = "Railroad",
                        "7" = "Arson",
                        "8" = "Playing With Fire",
                        "9" = "Miscellaneous",
                        "10" = "Vehicle",
                        "11" = "Powerline",
                        "12" = "Firefighter Training",
                        "13" = "Non-Firefighter Training",
                        "14" = "Unidentified",
                        "15" = "Structure",
                        "16" = "Aircraft",
                        "17" = "Volcanic",
                        "18" = "Escaped Prescribed Burn",
                        "19" = "Illegal Alien Campfire"
                        ))
```

##Exploratory Data Analysis
```{r theme set}
#I'm not sure if you have preferences for theme, but we should set it here so that all the plots match

mytheme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),legend.position = "top", 
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
theme_set(mytheme)
```

```{r histogram of fire counts}
#I was just messing around, let me know what you think of this! And the colors!
fire_count_plot <- CA_fires %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year)) + 
  labs( x = "Year",
        y = "Number of Fires",
        title = "Changes in Fire Occurence Over Time") + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1,
                 fill = 'sienna3',
                 color = 'darkred') + 
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 7)

print(fire_count_plot)
```

```{r histogram of fire burn areas}
fire_size_plot <- CA_fires %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y=GIS.Calculated.Acres, x=Year)) + 
  geom_point(color = 'darkred') + 
  labs(y="Burn Acreage Calculated in GIS")
```
